headline: Spatial transcriptomics workflows, benchmarks and atlases broaden cross-platform analysis
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Tools And Atlases
summary: Multi-platform spatial data now span many technologies, species and time points, making standardized reanalysis and segmentation benchmarking pressing.
synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure for spatial transcriptomics. Spatialsnake provides a SpatialData and Snakemake workflow for processed Visium, Visium HD, Stereo-seq, Xenium and MERFISH outputs, while a benchmark evaluates 11 image-, transcriptomics- and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets from five technologies. Curated resources extend this to scale: SpatialRegNet quantifies spot-level activity of 6733 TF regulon networks across 1322 human and mouse slices, 4D-atlas standardizes 1629 slices across 88 time points and six species, and scSpatial curates over 1800 sections from 630 projects. Cell3D adds interactive 2D/3D visualization and crosstalk analysis. Separately, donor-aware reanalysis of 15q13.3-deletion organoids, a distal radius cartilage atlas, and knee OA scRNA-seq studies apply single-cell profiling to specific tissue and disease questions; the OA findings are candidate mechanisms rather than causal evidence. What is new is the convergence of standardized, multi-technology spatial data with regulon-level and time-resolved analysis.
